title: Sovereign Citizens are Idiots - Here's Why!
summary: A Missouri appellate lawyer explains why the not-driving-but-traveling argument fails and what happens when people refuse to identify or exit at traffic stops.

assertions.quote: indeed the constitution does say you have a right to travel but it doesn't say that you can drive without a license
in order to travel you're driving a car so certainly you are driving
driving is a privilege it's not a right you don't find it in the constitution

verdicts.note: Federal and state courts uniformly uphold licensing and registration requirements under the police power.
US Supreme Court: a state may require registration of motor vehicles and licensing of drivers with reasonable fees as an exercise of the police power, including for interstate travellers.
The Ohio appeals court restates that driving is a privilege the state can regulate and affirms convictions for no license display and no plate despite right-to-travel arguments.

A NZ court struck out a freeman's challenge to registration and licence requirements: anyone driving on public roads must follow vehicle legislation. This is a non-US ruling, not a US police-power holding.

assertions.quote: if you don't they are going to detain you put you in the back patrol car take you to jail and fingerprint it

verdicts.note: Drivers must produce a licence; refusing typically leads to arrest or citation, not release.

assertions.quote: you wind up missing a window and probably with a rather significant ticket obstruction of a police officer

verdicts.note: Widely documented stops end with broken windows, arrest, impound and obstruction or resisting charges, though some end with a ticket.
